e:
PSALM 71

Psa 71:1-24. The Psalmist, probably in old age, appeals to God for help from his enemies, pleading his past favors, and stating his present need; and, in confidence of a hearing, he promises his grateful thanks and praise.

1-3. (Compare Psa 30:1-3). 3. given commandment--literally, "ordained," as in Psa 44:4; 68:28. rock ... fortress--(Psa 18:2).
4-5. cruel man--corrupt and ill-natured--literally, "sour." 5. trust--place of trust.

6-9. His history from early infancy illustrated God's care, and his wonderful deliverances were at once occasions of praise and ground of confidence for the future. my praise ... of thee--literally, "in" or "by Thee" (Psa 22:25).
10-11. The craft and malicious taunts of his enemies now led him to call for aid (compare the terms used, 2Sa 17:12; Psa 3:2; 7:2).

14-16. The ruin of his enemies, as illustrating God's faithfulness, is his deliverance, and a reason for future confidence. 15. for I know ... thereof--innumerable, as he had not time to count them. 16. in the strength--or, relying on it. thy righteousness--or, faithful performance of promises to the pious (Psa 7:17; 31:1).

17-21. Past experience again encourages. taught me, &c.--by providential dealings. 19. is very high--distinguished (Psa 36:5; Is 55:9). 20. depths of the earth--debased, low condition. 21. increase, &c.--that is, the great things done for me (Psa 71:19; compare Psa 40:5).
22-24. To the occasion of praise he now adds the promise to render it. will ... praise--literally, "will thank." even thy truth--as to Thy truth or faithfulness.
